subject: literature
passage: Lady Ashcombe had presided over a great many embassy dinners, and she prided herself on never allowing a conversation to falter. When the Austrian envoy and the French attaché began to quarrel over the soup, she neither rebuked them nor pretended not to hear; she merely remarked upon the unseasonable warmth of the evening, and so deftly did she draw first one man and then the other into agreement about the weather that, by the fish course, the two were laughing together. Her guests departed marveling at a hostess who could ______ a dispute without ever appearing to notice it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Lady Ashcombe turns the quarrel into laughter by steering the men to a harmless topic, without scolding them and without seeming to notice the argument. The blank must mean calming a conflict before it grows, which is what "defuse" means.
explanation.A: Correct. To defuse a dispute is to reduce its tension. By the fish course the quarreling men "were laughing together," thanks to her quiet steering.
explanation.B: Incorrect. She did not ignore the quarrel; the text says she did not pretend "not to hear" and instead acted to end it. She only appeared not to notice it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. To exacerbate a dispute is to make it worse, but the quarrel ends in laughter.
explanation.D: Incorrect. To adjudicate is to judge between two sides. Lady Ashcombe never decides who is right; she "neither rebuked them" and simply changes the subject.
